pages.text:
Virtual Event:

SECURITYWEEK NETWORK:
ICS:
Hi, what are you looking for?
A suspected state-sponsored threat actor exploited multiple Fortinet vulnerabilities in an attack against a telecommunications organization, Palo Alto Networks reports.
The intrusion, attributed to UNC5820 (tracked by Palo Alto Networks as CL-STA-0954), occurred in September 2024 and resulted in long-term access to the victim’s environment.
Initial access was obtained through the exploitation of a critical remote code execution (RCE) bug in FortiManager, tracked as CVE-2024-47575 and patched in October 2024 as a zero-day.
Shortly after the patches were rolled out, Mandiant warned that UNC5820 had been exploiting the flaw, named FortiJump, since at least June 2024.
A fresh report from Palo Alto Networks shows that UNC5820 also exploited CVE-2025-61624, a path traversal vulnerability affecting multiple Fortinet products, as part of the same intrusion.
Impacting FortiOS, FortiPAM, FortiProxy, and FortiSwitchManager and patched in April 2026, the security defect could allow authenticated attackers to write or delete arbitrary files. Fortinet flagged its exploitation as a zero-day at the time of disclosure.
Advertisement. Scroll to continue reading.
On Friday, the US cybersecurity agency CISA added CVE-2025-61624 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) list, urging federal agencies to patch it immediately.
UNC5820 appears to have exploited the path traversal as a zero-day to deploy a previously unknown FortiGate implant dubbed PeerStitch.
The ARM64 malware resides in memory, avoids opening listening ports or initiating outbound network connections, and communicates through the traffic generated by legitimate processes on the appliance.
As part of the observed attack, UNC5820 exploited FortiJump to access a central FortiManager instance, registered a rogue Virtual FortiGate appliance, and exfiltrated a configuration archive containing details on FortiManager, more than 500 managed FortiGate firewalls, and the victim’s network.
UNC5820 exploited CVE-2025-61624 to gain root access to the underlying firewall operating system, dropping a script to initiate the PeerStitch deployment.
Written in C, the implant acts as a ‘one-shot process memory patching injector’ targeting the central system and traffic logging, and the IKE/IPsec VPN service daemons in FortiOS to create a covert, memory-resident communication bridge between them and bypass default FortiOS security validations.
As part of the attack, the threat actor was also seen impersonating FortiManager in FortiGate-to-FortiManager (FGFM) communications to issue commands from external infrastructure and “took extensive measures to eliminate forensic artifacts”.
According to Palo Alto Networks, UNC5820 asserted the management identity either by terminating the authentic FortiManager’s session by exploiting CVE-2024-26008, or by reusing exfiltrated secrets and authenticating as the legitimate FortiManager.
“The discovery of the PeerStitch implant demonstrates the increasing technical maturity of edge-device malware. By operating as a one-shot injector, avoiding persistent disk artifacts and building a covert inter-process communication bridge inside process memory, the attackers achieved sustained persistence while evading traditional monitoring,” Palo Alto Networks notes.

Fortinet, Inc. (NASDAQ:FTNT) and CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ:CRWD) each reported roughly 26% revenue growth in their latest quarters. Investors nevertheless pay about 53 times Fortinet’s current-year adjusted earnings guidance and 215 times CrowdStrike’s. The gap raises a useful question: how much more should durable subscription growth cost when the cheaper company already earns substantial reported profits?
The multiples use October 2 closing prices of $180.95 and $270.04, divided by guidance midpoints of $3.44 and $1.255. Fortinet’s year ends December 2026; CrowdStrike’s ends January 2027. CrowdStrike’s price and earnings are both adjusted for July’s four-for-one split. Our earlier CrowdStrike–Palo Alto valuation comparison tests a different rival; Fortinet adds a sharper hardware-versus-subscription challenge.
The same growth rate hides different engines
Fortinet’s June-quarter product revenue jumped 52%, while services grew 14%. Hardware demand can arrive in bursts as customers upgrade networks.Converting the product surge into recurring service revenue would make growth more durable when the hardware upgrade cycle slows. That matters when judging the businesses in our high-growth, low-debt stock screen: financial flexibility and growth durability answer different questions.
CrowdStrike’s July-quarter ending annual recurring revenue grew 25% to $5.84 billion. Net new ARR increased 51% to $333 million, supporting a case for accelerating customer commitments. Its security platform spans endpoints, identity and cloud workloads. Our agentic-AI stock shortlist examines where security fits among the platforms companies need as automated work spreads.
Fortinet is also expanding beyond appliances. Management reported 35% billings growth in Unified SASE, which combines networking and security services, and 25% in AI-driven Security Operations. These are billings measures, not recognized revenue. The premium requires more durable, profitable growth. Our analysis of cybersecurity’s split from the AI infrastructure trade asks why security budgets might follow a different spending cycle.
Insider Monkey’s Q2 2026 holder count rose to 62 from 52 in Q1 for Fortinet and to 89 from 79 for CrowdStrike. Arrowstreet increased Fortinet shares about 5%; D. E. Shaw increased CrowdStrike shares 18%. The competing business models both drew broader fund ownership.
Reported profits change the burden of proof
Fortinet earned a 33.7% GAAP operating margin in Q2. CrowdStrike recorded a $33.2 million GAAP operating loss on $1.47 billion of revenue, despite substantial adjusted profit. CrowdStrike’s reconciliation adds back $399 million of stock compensation and related payroll taxes, about 27% of revenue. That makes a fourfold adjusted-earnings multiple gap especially demanding.
Cash flow provides a second lens. Fortinet generated reported $966 million of free cash flow, or 47.2% of revenue, while CrowdStrike reported $377 million, or about 26%; their free-cash-flow definitions differ. Collections and working capital make one quarter an imperfect comparison, and stock compensation can support cash flow while diluting shareholders. Our cash-flow screen that includes Fortinet examines that distinction; our return-on-equity ranking shows why high reported profitability also needs a balance-sheet check.
CrowdStrike’s strongest defense is a longer growth runway. Security agents could increase the value of its installed platform and proprietary customer context. The commercial question behind its cybersecurity work with Nvidia is whether that advantage becomes incremental revenue. Its expanded OpenAI partnership presents a related test: better models must strengthen pricing power enough to offset competition and deployment costs.
How much execution does the premium require?
As an illustration, if Fortinet’s adjusted earnings per share grew 15% annually for five years with both share prices unchanged, CrowdStrike would need roughly 52% annual earnings-per-share growth to reach Fortinet’s resulting multiple of about 26 times earnings. This is a valuation sensitivity, not a forecast; faster Fortinet growth would raise the hurdle. CrowdStrike can outperform without fully closing the gap, but continued premium pricing carries risk.
CrowdStrike’s September 15 short interest was 27.93 million shares, approximately 2.8% of float, with 2.42 days to cover. That dated snapshot offers limited support for a squeeze thesis.
Fortinet is my relative preference, though 53 times guided earnings still requires sustained growth. I would reconsider if its service growth stalls while CrowdStrike converts rising ARR into much faster per-share profits with less dilution. The risk explored in our analysis of AI and cybersecurity moats matters to both: stronger tools can expand demand while narrowing product differences. CrowdStrike must monetize that change exceptionally well to justify today’s price.

CBTS and Fortinet Launch Fully Managed Secure Networking Service for Growing Mid-Market Organizations
Tue, October 20, 2026 at 8:00 AM CDT 5 min read
New CBTS service brings networking and security into one platform, managed 24x7 for organizations with lean IT teams
CBTS brings firewalls, switching, wireless, and SD-WAN onto a single Fortinet platform that CBTS designs, deploys, and operates.
The service is built for mid-market and multi-site organizations that need stronger networking and security capabilities, without adding specialized in-house staff.
CBTS brings Fortinet-certified engineers, proven reference architectures, and 24x7 operations under one accountable team and one monthly subscription.
CINCINNATI, October 20, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--CBTS, a leading North American technology services company, today launched CBTS Fortinet Managed Services. The new fully managed secure networking service helps mid-market and multi-site organizations modernize aging infrastructure, strengthen security, and support growth without adding network and security headcount.
Mid-market organizations are caught between the sophistication of today's threats and the resources available to defend against a growing attack surface. According to Forrester Research, security and risk leaders entering the 2027 planning cycle face persistent challenges, including platform sprawl, talent scarcity, rising costs, and growing pressure from AI-enabled threats. As adversaries gain access to more advanced AI capabilities, already-stretched security teams will face greater pressure to detect and respond to threats quickly.1
Chris DeBrunner, CISO at CBTS, said: "For most mid-market organizations, hiring their way out of the problem is no longer realistic. CBTS gives them another option: bring networking and security together on a single platform, operated by certified CBTS engineers 24 hours a day."
One platform, one partner, with one predictable cost
Aging switches, firewalls, and wireless infrastructure make that gap even harder to close. When those technologies sit across disconnected platforms, modernization can introduce even more tools, policies, and operational complexity.
CBTS addresses this by bringing Fortinet firewalls, switching, wireless, and SD-WAN onto a single platform, with CBTS responsible for assessment, design, deployment, and 24x7 operations. The common operating model gives organizations a more consistent network and security foundation as AI increases the speed and complexity of cyber threats. Clients receive the technology and ongoing management through one subscription, giving lean IT teams a single accountable partner for network performance and security.
The model is designed around three areas of simplification:
One platform: Networking and security operate under a common architecture and policy model, reducing the gaps created by disconnected technologies.
One partner: The same Fortinet-certified CBTS engineers that design the environment support its ongoing operations, reducing handoffs between resellers, integrators, and managed service providers.
One predictable cost: Hardware, deployment, management, and ongoing refresh are combined into a predictable monthly operating cost with no upfront capital investment.
"Fortinet converges networking and security into a unified platform, and CBTS brings the engineering expertise and managed services capabilities to put that platform to work for clients," said Michael O'Brien, US RVP of Carrier Services, Fortinet. "Together, we are giving mid-market organizations a simpler way to modernize their networks, with one team supporting the environment from design and deployment through ongoing operations."
Built for mid-market, multi-site organizations
CBTS Fortinet Managed Services is designed for multi-site organizations across industries including healthcare, retail and food service, financial services, manufacturing, consumer packaged goods.
Centralized network and security management gives those organizations a more consistent way to open new locations, maintain policy across sites, and modernize infrastructure without building a larger internal engineering function. The subscription model also combines hardware refresh and ongoing management into a single predictable monthly cost rather than a series of separate technology investments.
Fortinet managed services proven at scale
CBTS has already put this model into practice for a quick-service restaurant chain with over 100 locations, replacing a mixed-vendor network with a single, fully managed Fortinet platform. The new environment brings firewall, wireless, switching, and SD-WAN under one managed service, reducing cost and complexity while creating room for future growth.
The client's environment is managed through a dedicated dashboard, providing visibility into its network while maintaining separation from other managed environments.
CBTS is a Fortinet Expert-tier partner with certified engineers who design, deploy, and manage Fortinet environments. CBTS Fortinet Managed Services is available across North America now.
Organizations do not need to be on Fortinet today to benefit. The CBTS service includes migration, with a dedicated project manager keeping the transition seamless. CBTS can also show how Fortinet integrates with their existing technology and third-party solutions.
Learn more about CBTS Fortinet Managed Services.

Offering expertise in AI, data, applications, platforms, and security, CBTS combines the technical depth of a large integrator with the flexibility and client focus of a specialized partner. Founded in 1994 and headquartered in Cincinnati, Ohio, CBTS and its OnX Canada division serve more than 3,000 clients. CBTS has been named CRN Tech Elite 250 for seven consecutive years and ranks #49 on the CRN Solution Provider 500. Learn more at cbts.com.
Fortinet (NASDAQ: FTNT) is a driving force in the evolution of cybersecurity and the convergence of networking and security. Our mission is to secure people, devices, and data everywhere, and today we deliver cybersecurity everywhere our customers need it with the largest integrated portfolio of over 50 enterprise-grade products. Well over half a million customers trust Fortinet's solutions, which are among the most deployed, most patented, and most validated in the industry. The Fortinet Training Institute, one of the largest and broadest training programs in the industry, is dedicated to making cybersecurity training and new career opportunities available to everyone. Collaboration with esteemed organizations from both the public and private sectors, including Computer Emergency Response Teams ("CERTS"), government entities, and academia, is a fundamental aspect of Fortinet's commitment to enhance cyber resilience globally. FortiGuard Labs, Fortinet's elite threat intelligence and research organization, develops and utilizes leading-edge machine learning and AI technologies to provide customers with timely and consistently top-rated protection and actionable threat intelligence. Learn more at https://www.fortinet.com, the Fortinet Blog, and FortiGuard Labs.

Can Fortinet's SASE Momentum Propel the Stock to New Highs?

Fortinet FTNT is gaining traction with its push to converge firewall and secure access service edge (SASE) technologies, positioning the stock for upside. At its SASE Summit 2026, highlighted on Oct. 8, the company outlined how its Unified SASE platform is evolving to secure AI applications and autonomous agents alongside human users.
Fortinet is addressing sovereignty demands through FortiSASE Outpost, which extends inspection and enforcement to on-premises and colocation sites under centralized cloud management, and FortiSASE Sovereign, a private SASE model that customers or service providers can run on their infrastructure.
This builds on the FortiGate 1200G series launched with FortiSASE Outpost in July, which combines ASIC-powered local enforcement with cloud-delivered security. The strategy is showing up in results. In second-quarter 2026, the combined SASE Firewall business, spanning Secure Networking and Unified SASE, grew 34% to more than $2 billion. Unified SASE billings rose 35%, while FortiSASE billings more than doubled. Billings jumped 33% year over year to $2.37 billion, and revenues climbed 26% to $2.05 billion, exceeding the high end of guidance.
Fundamentals reinforce the outlook. Product revenues surged 52% to $773 million, with management expecting attached services to boost service revenue growth in the second half. Meanwhile, the non-GAAP operating margin hit a second-quarter record of 38%.
Backed by this momentum, Fortinet raised its 2026 outlook and now expects revenues of $8.02-$8.18 billion, implying 19% growth, billings of $9.35-$9.55 billion and service revenues of $5.18-$5.22 billion. Non-GAAP operating margin is projected at 35-37%, with non-GAAP EPS of $3.41-$3.47. For the third quarter, it expects revenues of $2.01-$2.10 billion, billings of $2.25-$2.35 billion and non-GAAP EPS of 83-87 cents.
With SASE emerging as a growth engine and guidance pointing to sustained billings strength, Fortinet appears well placed to extend its momentum, paving the way for the stock to reach new highs.

Fortinet faces competition in SASE from Palo Alto Networks PANW and Zscaler ZS. Palo Alto Networks' Next-Generation Security ARR, which includes SASE, grew 63% to $9.10 billion in fiscal fourth-quarter 2026, while SASE competitive displacements totaled about $450 million for the fiscal year.
Palo Alto Networks expects fiscal 2027 NGS ARR of $11.08-$11.18 billion. Zscaler, a cloud-native zero-trust provider, grew ARR 25% to $3.77 billion in the same quarter and ended with more than 950 Zero Trust Everywhere enterprises. Zscaler projects fiscal 2027 ARR of $4.40-$4.43 billion. Unlike Zscaler's cloud-delivered approach, Fortinet offers on-premises, hybrid and sovereign SASE deployments.
FTNT's Share Price Performance, Valuation & Estimates
Fortinet shares have gained 116% in the year-to-date period, outperforming the Zacks Security industry and the broader Computer and Technology sector's growth of 81.8% and 15.8%, respectively.

NET vs. FTNT: Which Cybersecurity Stock Should You Buy Right Now?
Wed, October 14, 2026 at 7:42 AM CDT 5 min read
Cloudflare NET and Fortinet Inc. FTNT are well-known players in the cybersecurity domain. While Cloudflare provides a cloud-native platform spanning network security, application security and connectivity, Fortinet combines a variety of hardware and cloud-based security solutions.
Both NET and FTNT are riding key industry trends, driven by the mounting incidents of credential theft, remote desktop protocol breaches and social engineering-based strikes by malicious actors. However, from an investment perspective, one stock offers a more favorable outlook than the other right now. Let's break down their fundamentals, growth prospects, market challenges and valuation to determine which stock offers a more compelling investment case.
Cloudflare is seeing stronger demand for its SASE and Zero Trust offerings as companies look to adopt AI more securely. Management said the key reason big companies are approaching Cloudflare is that they know they need AI but want to deploy it securely. This is creating new opportunities for the company's SASE and Zero Trust platforms, particularly as enterprises need to secure AI agents in addition to human users.
Cloudflare believes its developer-focused approach gives it an advantage in this market. Management said companies will have more AI agents working across their organizations and will need a security model designed for these agents. In one example, a large U.K. government agency was evaluating a first-generation Zero Trust provider but reconsidered the project after discussing its plans for AI agents with Cloudflare. Management said the agency canceled its existing request for proposal and is now reevaluating the project with an agents-first approach. Cloudflare believes its developer-focused approach has helped its SASE and Zero Trust platforms gain significant share over the past six months.
However, Cloudflare's non-GAAP gross margin was 73.1% in the second quarter of 2026, down 320 basis points from 76.3% a year ago. The main issue is the changing mix of traffic on Cloudflare's network. As paid traffic grows relative to free traffic, a larger portion of Cloudflare's network costs is being allocated to cost of revenue. This shows that Cloudflare is handling more traffic that requires infrastructure and network resources, putting pressure on gross margins.
This is particularly relevant as AI workloads and machine-to-machine traffic expand. These workloads can drive more usage and revenues, but they also require Cloudflare to provide more compute, network and storage capacity. Although management expects gross-margin pressure to stabilize, continued growth in AI and developer workloads could require higher infrastructure spending. This could limit near-term margin expansion even as revenues continue to grow rapidly.
Fortinet is seeing strong demand for its SASE Firewall as enterprises upgrade network security to support AI workloads, cloud environments and distributed workforces. In the second quarter of 2026, Fortinet's SASE Firewall business grew 34% to more than $2 billion. Unified SASE billings increased 35%, while FortiSASE billings grew more than 100% year over year. FortiSASE adoption also reached 90% of Fortinet's large-enterprise installed base.
Fortinet believes its SASE Firewall can address a larger market than cloud-only SASE solutions. The company combines firewall, SASE and hybrid mesh capabilities on its FortiOS platform and supports both cloud and on-premises deployments. Management believes this opportunity could be two to three times larger than the cloud-only SASE market. Demand for sovereign SASE is also increasing as enterprises and service providers look for better data privacy, local processing and performance.
AI is adding another growth driver. As AI applications increase machine-to-machine and data-center traffic, customers need better visibility and control over network traffic. Fortinet said AI is accelerating the convergence of networking and security. The company is also seeing AI data center wins, including an eight-figure deal with a cloud provider offering generative AI infrastructure.
The growth in SASE could also support Fortinet's financial performance. Product revenues increased 52% year over year in the second quarter of 2026, while service revenues grew 14% year over year. Service billings increased 26% year over year, and management expects service revenue growth to improve in the second half of 2026. New SASE and SD-WAN services can add to Fortinet's recurring service revenues as customers expand their deployments. With strong SASE demand, AI-driven security needs and growing adoption of sovereign SASE, the SASE Firewall could become an important driver of Fortinet's product and service revenue growth.
How do Earnings Estimates Compare for NET & FTNT?
The Zacks Consensus Estimate for NET's 2026 and 2027 EPS is pinned at $1.26 and $1.72, respectively. The estimates for fiscal 2026 and 2027 have remained unchanged over the past 30 days.
The Zacks Consensus Estimate for FTNT's 2026 and 2027 EPS is pegged at $3.45 and $3.85, respectively. The estimates for 2026 and 2027 have both been revised up by 3 cents over the past 30 days.

Year to date, shares of NET and FTNT have surged 76.6% and 140.2%, respectively.

Currently, FTNT is trading at a forward sales multiple of 15.77X, significantly lower than NET's forward sales multiple of 34.93X. FTNT's reasonable valuation makes it more attractive for investors looking for value and stability.

Conclusion: Buy FTNT, Sell NET Right Now
Both Cloudflare and Fortinet are key players in the cybersecurity space. However, Cloudflare's gross margins remain under pressure as higher paid traffic and AI workload usage increase infrastructure costs. In contrast, Fortinet shows steadier execution, with strong adoption of FortiSASE, Unified SASE and sovereign SASE. Further, FTNT's reasonable valuation offers some downside protection as well, making the stock an attractive buy, particularly for investors seeking exposure to cybersecurity growth at a fair price.

It will also align joint business development, customer engagement, service delivery and competitive commercial terms globally to address organizations' growing cybersecurity challenges.
Clients contend with escalating cyber threats and ransomware attacks, increasingly complex digital environments, expanding digital transformation programs, stricter regulatory requirements and a persistent shortage of cybersecurity skills. The strengthened Atos Fortinet partnership will combine advanced security technologies with managed security capabilities on a global scale.
Through integrated solutions and consistent services worldwide, the partnership will enable organizations to enhance protection and visibility across cloud and on-premises environments, simplify security operations, accelerate threat detection and remediation, and gain the scalability and flexibility required to pursue their digital transformation securely.
Fortinet's advanced cybersecurity technologies and engagement support across geographies and Atos' extensive expertise in managed security services, consulting and integration, as well as its global delivery capabilities and network of Security Operations Centers, will provide organizations with more innovative and scalable services to strengthen cyber resilience and support secure digital transformation, with a direct impact on operational efficiency. By combining Fortinet's advanced cybersecurity technologies with Atos' consulting, integration and managed security expertise, we can provide consistent and scalable protection across hybrid and multi-cloud environments and help clients address the security challenges in the AI era."

Fortinet, Inc. (NASDAQ:FTNT) and CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ:CRWD) each reported roughly 26% revenue growth in their latest quarters. Investors nevertheless pay about 53 times Fortinet’s current-year adjusted earnings guidance and 215 times CrowdStrike’s. The gap raises a useful question: how much more should durable subscription growth cost when the cheaper company already earns substantial reported profits?
The multiples use October 2 closing prices of $180.95 and $270.04, divided by guidance midpoints of $3.44 and $1.255. Fortinet’s year ends December 2026; CrowdStrike’s ends January 2027. CrowdStrike’s price and earnings are both adjusted for July’s four-for-one split. Our earlier CrowdStrike–Palo Alto valuation comparison tests a different rival; Fortinet adds a sharper hardware-versus-subscription challenge.
The same growth rate hides different engines
Fortinet’s June-quarter product revenue jumped 52%, while services grew 14%. Hardware demand can arrive in bursts as customers upgrade networks.Converting the product surge into recurring service revenue would make growth more durable when the hardware upgrade cycle slows. That matters when judging the businesses in our high-growth, low-debt stock screen: financial flexibility and growth durability answer different questions.
CrowdStrike’s July-quarter ending annual recurring revenue grew 25% to $5.84 billion. Net new ARR increased 51% to $333 million, supporting a case for accelerating customer commitments. Its security platform spans endpoints, identity and cloud workloads. Our agentic-AI stock shortlist examines where security fits among the platforms companies need as automated work spreads.
Fortinet is also expanding beyond appliances. Management reported 35% billings growth in Unified SASE, which combines networking and security services, and 25% in AI-driven Security Operations. These are billings measures, not recognized revenue. The premium requires more durable, profitable growth. Our analysis of cybersecurity’s split from the AI infrastructure trade asks why security budgets might follow a different spending cycle.
Insider Monkey’s Q2 2026 holder count rose to 62 from 52 in Q1 for Fortinet and to 89 from 79 for CrowdStrike. Arrowstreet increased Fortinet shares about 5%; D. E. Shaw increased CrowdStrike shares 18%. The competing business models both drew broader fund ownership.
Reported profits change the burden of proof
Fortinet earned a 33.7% GAAP operating margin in Q2. CrowdStrike recorded a $33.2 million GAAP operating loss on $1.47 billion of revenue, despite substantial adjusted profit. CrowdStrike’s reconciliation adds back $399 million of stock compensation and related payroll taxes, about 27% of revenue. That makes a fourfold adjusted-earnings multiple gap especially demanding.
Cash flow provides a second lens. Fortinet generated reported $966 million of free cash flow, or 47.2% of revenue, while CrowdStrike reported $377 million, or about 26%; their free-cash-flow definitions differ. Collections and working capital make one quarter an imperfect comparison, and stock compensation can support cash flow while diluting shareholders. Our cash-flow screen that includes Fortinet examines that distinction; our return-on-equity ranking shows why high reported profitability also needs a balance-sheet check.
CrowdStrike’s strongest defense is a longer growth runway. Security agents could increase the value of its installed platform and proprietary customer context. The commercial question behind its cybersecurity work with Nvidia is whether that advantage becomes incremental revenue. Its expanded OpenAI partnership presents a related test: better models must strengthen pricing power enough to offset competition and deployment costs.
How much execution does the premium require?
As an illustration, if Fortinet’s adjusted earnings per share grew 15% annually for five years with both share prices unchanged, CrowdStrike would need roughly 52% annual earnings-per-share growth to reach Fortinet’s resulting multiple of about 26 times earnings. This is a valuation sensitivity, not a forecast; faster Fortinet growth would raise the hurdle. CrowdStrike can outperform without fully closing the gap, but continued premium pricing carries risk.
CrowdStrike’s September 15 short interest was 27.93 million shares, approximately 2.8% of float, with 2.42 days to cover. That dated snapshot offers limited support for a squeeze thesis.
Fortinet is my relative preference, though 53 times guided earnings still requires sustained growth. I would reconsider if its service growth stalls while CrowdStrike converts rising ARR into much faster per-share profits with less dilution. The risk explored in our analysis of AI and cybersecurity moats matters to both: stronger tools can expand demand while narrowing product differences. CrowdStrike must monetize that change exceptionally well to justify today’s price.

At its SASE Summit 2026, highlighted on Oct. 8, the company outlined how its Unified SASE platform is evolving to secure AI applications and autonomous agents alongside human users.
Fortinet is addressing sovereignty demands through FortiSASE Outpost, which extends inspection and enforcement to on-premises and colocation sites under centralized cloud management, and FortiSASE Sovereign, a private SASE model that customers or service providers can run on their infrastructure.
This builds on the FortiGate 1200G series launched with FortiSASE Outpost in July, which combines ASIC-powered local enforcement with cloud-delivered security. The strategy is showing up in results. NET vs. FTNT: Which Cybersecurity Stock Should You Buy Right Now?
Wed, October 14, 2026 at 7:42 AM CDT 5 min read
Cloudflare NET and Fortinet Inc. FTNT are well-known players in the cybersecurity domain. While Cloudflare provides a cloud-native platform spanning network security, application security and connectivity, Fortinet combines a variety of hardware and cloud-based security solutions.
Both NET and FTNT are riding key industry trends, driven by the mounting incidents of credential theft, remote desktop protocol breaches and social engineering-based strikes by malicious actors. However, from an investment perspective, one stock offers a more favorable outlook than the other right now. Let's break down their fundamentals, growth prospects, market challenges and valuation to determine which stock offers a more compelling investment case.
Cloudflare is seeing stronger demand for its SASE and Zero Trust offerings as companies look to adopt AI more securely. Management said the key reason big companies are approaching Cloudflare is that they know they need AI but want to deploy it securely. This is creating new opportunities for the company's SASE and Zero Trust platforms, particularly as enterprises need to secure AI agents in addition to human users.
Cloudflare believes its developer-focused approach gives it an advantage in this market. Management said companies will have more AI agents working across their organizations and will need a security model designed for these agents. In one example, a large U.K. government agency was evaluating a first-generation Zero Trust provider but reconsidered the project after discussing its plans for AI agents with Cloudflare. Management said the agency canceled its existing request for proposal and is now reevaluating the project with an agents-first approach. Cloudflare believes its developer-focused approach has helped its SASE and Zero Trust platforms gain significant share over the past six months.
However, Cloudflare's non-GAAP gross margin was 73.1% in the second quarter of 2026, down 320 basis points from 76.3% a year ago. The main issue is the changing mix of traffic on Cloudflare's network. As paid traffic grows relative to free traffic, a larger portion of Cloudflare's network costs is being allocated to cost of revenue. This shows that Cloudflare is handling more traffic that requires infrastructure and network resources, putting pressure on gross margins.
This is particularly relevant as AI workloads and machine-to-machine traffic expand. These workloads can drive more usage and revenues, but they also require Cloudflare to provide more compute, network and storage capacity. Although management expects gross-margin pressure to stabilize, continued growth in AI and developer workloads could require higher infrastructure spending. This could limit near-term margin expansion even as revenues continue to grow rapidly.
Fortinet is seeing strong demand for its SASE Firewall as enterprises upgrade network security to support AI workloads, cloud environments and distributed workforces. In the second quarter of 2026, Fortinet's SASE Firewall business grew 34% to more than $2 billion. Unified SASE billings increased 35%, while FortiSASE billings grew more than 100% year over year. FortiSASE adoption also reached 90% of Fortinet's large-enterprise installed base.
Fortinet believes its SASE Firewall can address a larger market than cloud-only SASE solutions. The company combines firewall, SASE and hybrid mesh capabilities on its FortiOS platform and supports both cloud and on-premises deployments. Management believes this opportunity could be two to three times larger than the cloud-only SASE market. Demand for sovereign SASE is also increasing as enterprises and service providers look for better data privacy, local processing and performance.
AI is adding another growth driver. As AI applications increase machine-to-machine and data-center traffic, customers need better visibility and control over network traffic. Fortinet said AI is accelerating the convergence of networking and security. The company is also seeing AI data center wins, including an eight-figure deal with a cloud provider offering generative AI infrastructure.
The growth in SASE could also support Fortinet's financial performance. Product revenues increased 52% year over year in the second quarter of 2026, while service revenues grew 14% year over year. Service billings increased 26% year over year, and management expects service revenue growth to improve in the second half of 2026. New SASE and SD-WAN services can add to Fortinet's recurring service revenues as customers expand their deployments. With strong SASE demand, AI-driven security needs and growing adoption of sovereign SASE, the SASE Firewall could become an important driver of Fortinet's product and service revenue growth.
